title: Lineage VII foundational body plan
scope: Foundational body plan of Lineage VII, the unsegmented soft-bodied lineage, including life mode as a branch-level axis and its ancestral state; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Lineage VII bodies are unsegmented and soft, without a rigid internal skeleton or a jointed exoskeleton.
Bodies are broadly bilateral and elongate along a single axis, in contrast with Lineage V's tri-radial organisation.
Movement is driven by muscular waves running along the body axis rather than by Lineage V's travelling margin waves.
The lineage occurs in water, soil, and other moist substrates.
Life mode varies by branch across three modes.
Filter branches draw suspended material from water, sessile or weakly mobile on submerged surfaces.
Substrate branches live inside material such as soil, mud, litter, sediment, and decaying matter, driving through it by muscular waves and processing it as they go.
Grazer branches move over exposed surfaces, feeding from them and relying on protective secretions.
Aquatic filter feeding is ancestral; substrate branches derived from filterers by invading sediment and soil, and grazer branches derived from substrate branches by emerging onto exposed surfaces.
Substrate branches own substrate turnover, complementing rather than duplicating the thread decomposers that wrap and digest concentrated dead material from outside.
Internal parasitism derives from the substrate habit.
boundaries: Filter branch, substrate branch, grazer branch, and muscular wave are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The plan establishes no worm, mollusc, snail, slug, leech, flatworm, or other Earth-clade homology and no direct Earth-animal transplant.
Species, names, sizes, proportions, colours, lifespans, and the branch inventory remain open.

Bilateral and axially elongate describe qualitative organisation only; they establish no fixed proportions, head, tail, or invariant external form, and derived branches may be secondarily reduced or asymmetric.

Whether any branch carries mineralised structures, shells, plates, or other hard parts remains open; softness describes the absence of a rigid internal skeleton and jointed exoskeleton, not the absence of all hard tissue.
Feeding mechanisms, digestion, senses, respiration, circulation, and internal organisation remain open across every branch.

Moisture dependence is a lineage tendency; exact desiccation, freezing, salinity, and compaction tolerances remain open, and no branch is established as unable to endure dry conditions in some resting state.
Substrate turnover is an ecological role, not a rate, yield, soil model, or guarantee that any particular ground is worked, fertile, or recoverable.
Protective secretions establish a functional adaptation only; their chemistry, effectiveness, toxicity, edibility, and any human use remain open.

Internal parasitism is available as a derived habit; no parasitic species, host, transmission route, symptom, prevalence, disease, treatment, or effect on any person, animal, or population is established.
The three modes describe life strategy only; they establish no fixed branch count, no exclusive niche assignment, and no rule that any niche belongs to one mode.
Ancestral filter feeding is an evolutionary-history claim establishing no timeline, transitional form, or surviving ancestral species.
No Lineage VII branch is established as present, abundant, or absent at any particular location, including the initial basin.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, universal creature level, spawn mechanism, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Earth life of any era and mythological creatures may inspire author-facing design; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted directly.
Moisture, oxygen, food, energy, materials, reproduction, disease, injury, mortality, and carrying capacity remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Digging, ploughing, butchery, flood deposits, and rot can uncover the lineage's hidden populations.
Submerged surfaces can carry filter branches and damp surfaces can carry grazers.
Soil fertility depends on invisible but load-bearing substrate turnover.
Internal parasites are biologically available, but every species, host, presence, and consequence requires its own evidence.
system_implications: The body plan describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, creature progression rule, spawn source, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What feeding, digestive, sensory, and respiratory mechanisms serve each branch mode?
Do any branches carry shells or other hard parts, and in which mode?
How do members reproduce and develop across the three modes?
Which parasitic branches exist, with what hosts and effects?
What substrate-turnover rates and soil consequences follow, and how do they interact with agriculture?
How do the lineage's moisture limits bound its range in the initial region?
sources: Author structural direction and selection on 2026-08-17

author_approval.evidence: After the life-mode cards were presented, the Author directed that all three modes be included as branches on one shared body plan, and selected 'A — Filter ancestral' for the ancestry question on 2026-08-17.
